_pine: needle atlas v4 (12 Nov): thin pinnate branchlets with comb rows of 16-18 mm needles and open sky between side twigs; alpha coverage per tile 0.31 / 0.39 (dense tips), 0.26-0.29 (open, young), 0.13-0.16 (narrow hanging, old, half dead); cards up to 60 cm, crossed in pairs, hanging twigs, sprays laid along the boughs. Within 2-3 m a spray is still a flat plane and reads fern- or cedar-like, and needles are drawn at 3 mm pitch, coarser than a real spruce

live boughs are now 5-10 cm thick (were up to 15 cm), but the inner third of each is still bare and rather straight, and the whorls are regular: from 20 m the tiers and bare boughs show as a ladder against the sky, and the crown is open rather than full
at distance the look depends on alpha-coverage-preserving mips (clip 0.25-0.33): with plain averaged mips the fronds will either fill in to blobs or vanish; untested in Unreal
it follows the sprite's full-skirted cone, so it reads as a spruce/fir-type conifer more than a long-trunked Scots pine
bark is a tiling scan in bands (no unique bake): knots are low geometric swellings without their own bark pattern; collars are a radius swell only
buttress roots are one surface with the bole and dive 0.18 m below the pivot, but the root ridges are smooth lobes and the thin root ends are tubes whose start is hidden inside the ridge
base soil/moss darkening is delivered as a UV-channel mask (UVMask.u) and a preview blend, not baked: the Unreal bark material has to use it
LOD0 is over the 8,000 soft target
wind colours, UVMask and custom normals are untested in Unreal
SM_Veg_Pine_Large_01: 24.2k triangles at LOD0 (cap 25k): no budget left for more spray cards; LOD1 12.8k
SM_Veg_Pine_Storm_01: the snapped top is a ring of long splinters and the fallen top is a small pine laid on its side with its underside flattened: there is no torn hinge of bark connecting the two
the fallen top widens the bounds to about 10 m; its position is fixed relative to the trunk
the most open of the pines: the bare-bough ladder is plain at 20 m
SM_Veg_Pine_Dry_01: dead needles come from the green v2 atlas recoloured and thinned in numpy, not from separately modelled dead sprays; with the finer fronds the dry tree is very open
bark is the pine scan desaturated to grey, not a scan of dead barkless wood
SM_Veg_Pine_Burnt_01: charred bark is the pine bark scan darkened with a procedural ash layer; no burnt-through hollows, no ember colour
limbs are simple broken tubes with a cap, not snapped splintered ends
SM_Veg_PineForestEdge_H_01: built from reduced pines; LOD0 now keeps 60 % of the sprays at 1.15x size (was 36 % at 1.5x, which read as broad leaves): 18.8k triangles. Still thinner-crowned than the single pines, lower trunks slender and bare; reviewed at 20 m only, not close
footprint about 10.5 x 5.5 m incl. crowns is my estimate from the sprite strip
SM_Veg_PineForestEdge_V_01: as the H module, LOD0 keeps 50 % of the sprays at 1.25x size: 21.4k triangles
footprint about 6.5 x 15 m incl. crowns, an estimate from sprites 32/09-10
_broadleaf: leaf cards are single bent planes; from directly below some are seen edge-on
limbs thinner than about 2 cm radius have no geometry (twigs are only what the atlas shows)
bark is a tiling scan in bands; knots are low swellings; buttress roots as on the pines (smooth lobes, tube ends)
base darkening is a UV-channel mask, not baked
wind colours, UVMask and custom normals are untested in Unreal
SM_Veg_Oak_Large_01: crown v4 (12 Nov): about 2.9k leaf-cluster cards of 0.46-0.78 m (first delivery: 1.3k of 0.85-1.25 m), three darker inner clusters per limb node, fewer sunlit tiles, crossed clusters on twigs standing 0.35-0.7 m clear of the outline; 16.3k triangles at LOD0, LOD1 4.6k (a large step)
single cards seen edge-on still show as thin streaks in places, and the leaves of one cluster are coplanar
value variation comes from three graded atlas tiles chosen by position; on the sunlit side the light tiles can still read as lighter patches
LOD2 (1.4k) uses 2.2x cards: clumps are plainly larger; meant for the far field only
SM_Veg_Oak_Large_02: as Oak_01 (16.5k triangles); broader and lower, larger in plan than the sprite suggests
SM_Veg_Willow_01: hanging withes are 0.5-0.6 m wide strips: inside the curtain looking up they fan visibly
willow leaf is a procedural texture, not a scan
SM_Veg_Willow_Large_01: long curtains are overlapping chained strips; where two strips overlap the foliage is denser in a band
still fuller than the sprite, which shows long bare dark limbs with separate drooping tiers
_dead: fine twigs are bare-twig alpha cards at the branch ends: close up they read as flat twig fans, and there are few of them against a real tree's thousands of twigs
bark is a re-tinted scan (willow bark darkened / oak bark paled), not a scan of dead wood; no broken stubs, cavities or peeling bark
buttress roots as on the other trees
SM_Veg_DeadTree_Frosted_01: frost is only a pale tint on bark and twigs; there is no snow lying on the limbs
_bush: v3 (12 Nov): 10-16 stems from a common stool, branches and twigs; every spray is a group of four small cards (0.15-0.3 m) at different depths, dark tiles inside and underneath, bare dead stems, gaps, long shoots; 3.5k-6.8k triangles at LOD0. The outline is ragged and sprawling rather than the sprite's round clipped bush
cards seen end-on still show as thin slivers or streaks in places; a few sunlit cards read as flat discs from the game camera
leaves are small (2.5-3 cm) because the 0.5 m spray tiles are used on small cards; the lobed leaf is a flat, evenly green scan and reads slightly graphic up close
dead stems arch low and one can lie across the ground in front of the bush (Wide); dead-twig cards at the foot read as flat brown fans from close
stems are 4-sided, branches 3-sided tubes with the dark bark set; no leaf litter or grass at the foot
two leaf types: ovate (LeafSet022) on Small and Round_Large, three-lobed (LeafSet029) on Round_Medium and Wide
new material MI_Veg_Shrub (T_Veg_Shrub_*) replaces MI_Veg_Understory on the four bushes and has to exist engine-side
wind colours and custom normals untested in Unreal
_ground: authored as separate tufts: the look depends on the terrain underneath and on scatter density
grass blades are real geometry with a centre crease at LOD0 only
blade strips and mushroom skins are procedural, not scans (no mushroom scan exists in the two allowed sources)
SM_Veg_Weed_Small_02: only six leaves, each a 2x4 quad grid: the broad dock leaves look a little like paddles at 1 m
SM_Veg_Flowers_01: petals are now geometry (13 cupped quads in two layers round a domed centre) but each petal is a two-quad strip textured from one painted petal
SM_Veg_Flowers_02: as Flowers_01; buttercup petals are five broad cupped quads with a procedural texture
SM_Veg_Mushroom_01: gills are a textured underside cone with a normal map, not separate plates; cap skin is procedural
real size (tallest about 13 cm), far smaller than the sprites
SM_Veg_Mushroom_02: as Mushroom_01; fly-agaric warts are painted, not raised
SM_Veg_GrassPatch_Dense_01: grass-clump alpha cards (about 30 per 0.9 m patch, 120 triangles): from above or at very low angles the fan shape of each clump card shows
the clump cards are modelled blades rendered to the understory atlas and then graded darker in numpy
meant to sit on a grass-coloured terrain; it does not hide bare ground on its own
SM_Veg_GrassPatch_Dense_02: as GrassPatch_Dense_01, with more dry blades
SM_Veg_Cabbage_01: 15 leaves from the dock-leaf scan cupped into a head: it reads as a leafy cabbage or lettuce, the leaves have no thick white ribs
SM_Veg_FlowerBed_Row_01: soil is the terrain agent's TransitionDirt set with a tint, world-scale UVs: it depends on that texture set being imported; the mound is a smooth three-ridge height field with no clods
plants are small dock / plantain rosettes in two rows, greener than the dark hedge-like sprite
_deadwood: bark and bare wood come from tiling bands, not a unique bake
moss is small low-poly cushions plus the texture's moss band: the cushions are few and still read as blobs at 1 m
snapped ends are bundles of thin 3-sided splinters
SM_Veg_Stump_01: root buttresses are now one surface with the bole and dive below ground, but they are smooth lobes
bark rim round the cut is a low uneven lip with a few peeled sections, not loose bark sheets
bracket fungi reuse the end-grain texture for their zoning
cut face is a planar scan projection, greyed, with extra procedural drying checks
SM_Veg_FallenLog_01: bark sheets are missing in four fixed patches (bare wood core shows, 1.4 cm step, no thickness wall at the hole edge)
the rot hollow is a short dark tube, with no crumbling rim or debris
SM_Veg_FallenBranch_Forked_01: thin parts are 4- and 5-sided tubes; bark scale on them is arbitrary
SM_Veg_TwigCluster_01: simple forked tubes; reads as twigs at gameplay distance only
SM_Veg_ThornBush_01: canes are 4-sided tubes with 3-sided thorn spikes: up close the canes are visibly faceted and all the same dark bark, with no dead leaves or berries
the tangle is arcs and loops from a formula, less knotted than the sprite
SM_Veg_ThornBranch_01: two short canes with thorns; very simple
SM_Veg_Fern_01: each frond is one bent alpha card (4 segments with a centre fold): the pinnae do not droop individually
frond texture is modelled from a procedural leaf, not a fern scan
SM_Veg_HangingVines_01: strands are chains of alpha cards (two crossed planes at LOD0) cut from two vine tiles: repetition along a strand can be spotted
pivot is on the floor and the strands hang from 2.8 m: it needs something above it to hang from
the sprite is almost leafless; these carry sparse leaves
_meadow: alpha cards carrying modelled blades (rendered atlas), not blade geometry: under about 1 m, blades in one card are coplanar and a card's bend line can show as a node across all its blades
blades are modelled (creased strips, vertex-colour gradient), not scanned; no clover, flowers or other herbs in the atlas
card normals point up so a carpet lights evenly: no per-blade specular glint
thin blades (2-6 mm = 2.5-8 texels) depend on alpha-coverage-preserving mips; untested in Unreal
new material MI_Veg_MeadowGrass has to be created engine-side; wind colours untested in Unreal
SM_Veg_GrassPatch_Tall_01: bounds are about 1.2-1.4 m because leaning cards overhang the 0.64 m root square
SM_Veg_GrassPatch_Dry_01: as Tall_01; dry tiles still contain about 10 % green blades
kinked dead blades are angular at the break
SM_Veg_GrassPatch_Short_01: single-quad cards 8-14 cm tall: from straight above the turf is mostly the terrain texture showing through
